# Monaco's AMD loader swallows mermaid's UMD define, so no diagram renders

## Context

@tobiu reported it with the diagnosis attached, which is why this is a leaf rather than an investigation:

```
loader.js:965 Uncaught Error: Can only have one anonymous define call per script file
    at c.enqueueDefineAnonymousModule (loader.js:965:11)
    at p (loader.js:1297:48)
    at mermaid.min.js:456:3421
Mermaid.mjs:66 Uncaught (in promise) ReferenceError: mermaid is not defined
    at Mermaid.loadFiles (Mermaid.mjs:66:9)
```

`loader.js` is **Monaco's AMD loader**, and it is in the stack *calling into* mermaid's `define`. Split off #18548, which owns the broader "a guide's diagram can be render-verified before merge" path and whose ACs span this repo and `neo-agent-skills`. This is the proximate defect underneath it.

## The Problem

`main.addon.Mermaid` loads `node_modules/mermaid/dist/mermaid.min.js` — the **UMD** bundle. UMD checks for `define.amd` before falling back to a global. `main.addon.MonacoEditor:129` loads Monaco's `loader.js`, which publishes exactly that `define`.

On any page carrying both, mermaid's anonymous `define` lands in Monaco's loader, which refuses it (`Can only have one anonymous define call per script file`). The library then never attaches to `window`, and `loadFiles` throws `mermaid is not defined` on the next line. Every diagram on the page fails.

Measured on the running portal, `dev @ bf4a73ce4b`:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `!!(window.define && window.define.amd)` on the guide route | **`true`** — the loader is present |
| `.neo-mermaid` containers | 4 |
| `.neo-mermaid svg` | **0** |

The portal is the surface where both libraries meet, which is why the symptom reads as portal-only.

**Regressed by `ffd860b664`** (2026-09-05, *"fix(monaco): restore editor initialization and lifecycle (#5822) (#18355)"*), which restructured `loadFiles` and its loader install. The Mermaid addon has not changed since January — the collision arrived from the other side.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/Mermaid.mjs` — `mermaidPath` points at `mermaid.min.js` (UMD); `loadFiles` uses `DomAccess.loadScript`; `loadFiles` and `render` both reach a **bare global** `mermaid`.
- `src/main/addon/MonacoEditor.mjs:129` — `await DomAccess.loadScript(path + '/loader.js')`.
- `node_modules/mermaid/dist/` ships `mermaid.esm.min.mjs`, and the package's own `exports` map resolves `.` to an ESM entry. **The UMD bundle is the one build we should not be using.**
- `src/util/HighlightJs.mjs:104` is the in-repo precedent for importing a library as a module: `await import(/* webpackIgnore: true */ path)`.

## The Fix

Import the ESM build instead of script-tagging the UMD one, and hold the library on the addon instead of on `window` — the same shape as `util.HighlightJs#hljs`. An ESM import has no `define` to find, so the conflict cannot occur regardless of load order.

**One trap this has to get right, and it is not obvious.** `Neo.config.basePath` is written for `DomAccess.loadScript`, whose `<script src>` resolves against the **document**. A dynamic `import()` resolves against the **importing module's own URL**, so a bare `basePath` from `src/main/addon/` resolves to `/src/node_modules/…` and 404s. The path must be resolved against `document.baseURI` explicitly, which also makes it depth-independent. (`HighlightJs` avoids this only because `src/util/` happens to sit at the depth its `../../` assumes — worth knowing before that file moves.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — a guide diagram renders as SVG on a page that also carries Monaco's AMD loader.** Asserted on the **rendered SVG**, never the container: the container is emitted from the fence alone and is present throughout the outage, so counting containers is precisely the assertion that would have stayed green.
- [ ] **AC-2 — the arm asserts Monaco's loader is present.** Without it, a future change that stopped loading Monaco on that route would make the arm pass by removing the conflict rather than by fixing it.
- [ ] **AC-3 — red-first, against the real defect.** Reverting only the addon change turns the arm red; restoring it returns green. Both directions, same arm.
- [ ] **AC-4 — the arm runs in CI.** Verified against the CI-shaped selection (`--list` with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` unset), not merely against a local run — most of the e2e tier does not run there.
- [ ] **AC-5 — no global `mermaid`.** The library is held on the addon; `git grep` finds no bare-global read left in the file. A UMD global is a name any other script on the page can collide with, which is the class of defect being removed.

## Out of Scope

- **#18548's verification path** — a documented, author-runnable render check with a deliberate-syntax-error control, plus the `guide-authoring` §3 corrections. Those ACs span `neo-agent-skills`; this ticket unblocks them by making the renderer work, and does not claim them.
- **Monaco's AMD loader itself.** It is global and will collide with the next UMD script someone loads. Removing that hazard means changing how Monaco is loaded, which is a far larger change with its own risk; recorded here as the residual it is.
- **Mermaid's reachability in a `dist` build.** `dist/` contains no mermaid and no build script copies it, so the `node_modules` path is a live question for a real deployment — separate from this dev-mode regression, and not made worse by it.
- **The portal instantiating guide content twice.** Measured in passing: 4 containers for 2 fences, in two identical pairs. Pre-existing, unrelated, noted so the next reader of that count is not surprised.

## Avoided Traps

- **Asserting the container exists.** #18548 names this explicitly: the container proves the fence parsed, not that anything rendered.
- **Concluding from a hidden pane.** Mermaid renders on layout, so an unlaid-out browser pane produces zero SVGs for a perfectly good fence — the reason the measurement above records a visible, sized viewport.
- **Keeping the UMD bundle and stashing `window.define` around the load.** It works, and it leaves the page with a global `mermaid` plus a load-order dependency that the next maintainer has to know about.

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## REOPENED — the fix was partial. The collision moved from load-time to chunk-load-time, and this ticket's title is still accurate.

@neo-opus-grace found it on merged `dev` and I reproduced it independently at `dev@87e3786673` before accepting:

```
route: tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout
containers: 2 | svg: 0 | defineAmd: true | livePreviews: 2
[error] Can only have one anonymous define call per script file
        at …/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs:6:203
```

Same error as the original report, from a different file.

## The mechanism, one level below what the ESM switch addressed

`mermaid.esm.min.mjs` is a 30 KB entry that lazily imports **206 chunks** from `dist/chunks/mermaid.esm.min/`. The entry has no `define` — which is why `loadFiles()` and `initialize()` now succeed and why my arm went green. A chunk still does, and it is **vendored `fastdom`**, not mermaid's own code:

```js
typeof define == "function" ? define(function(){return c}) : typeof H == "object" && (H.exports = c)
(typeof define)[0]  == "f"  ? define(function(){return r}) : (typeof N)[0]=="o" ? N.exports = r : window.fastdomPromised = r
```

⚠️ **Neither checks `define.amd`.** `grep -c 'define\.amd'` on that chunk returns **0**. They branch on `typeof define == "function"` alone, so *any* global `define` catches them — and they pass an **anonymous** factory, which is precisely what Monaco's loader refuses.

So the ESM switch removed the entry's registration and left a dependency's UMD wrapper to fire at **first render** instead of at load.

## Why my arm passed, and what it got wrong

@neo-opus-grace's diagnosis is exact and it corrects my own AC-2:

> The precondition asserts the loader is **present**. The defect needs the loader to be **busy**.

| route | mermaid fences | live-preview fences | `define.amd` | SVG |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` | 2 | **0** | `true` | **4/4** ✅ |
| `tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout` | 1 | **3** | `true` | **0/2** ❌ |

`define.amd` is `true` on both because the portal installs the loader app-wide. But on the guide route Monaco is loaded and **idle**, so no second anonymous `define` is ever in flight and the loader accepts mermaid's chunk silently. The route that breaks is the one where live previews instantiate editors.

**I measured one route and claimed a property of all of them.** The arm's precondition was the right instinct with the wrong predicate.

## Proposed fix, and the in-repo precedent

Hiding `window.define` around the render is **not viable**: chunks load asynchronously, and on exactly the routes that break, Monaco is concurrently loading modules — hiding `define` would trade a mermaid failure for a Monaco one.

The repository already solves "a third-party library with awkward packaging": `util.HighlightJs#load` imports from **`dist/highlight/highlight.custom.js`**, produced by the `build-highlightjs` script. A custom mermaid build under `dist/` would neutralise the vendored UMD wrappers at build time rather than fighting them at runtime.

It also closes the second, latent defect recorded on this ticket's Out of Scope: **`dist/` contains no mermaid and no build script copies one**, so today's `node_modules` path is unreachable in a real deployment. One artifact answers both.

## What must be true of the new arm

- [ ] It drives a route where Monaco is **busy**, not merely present — a live-preview route. The current `LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` targets the guide route and cannot reproduce this.
- [ ] The precondition asserts the discriminating condition, not the necessary one. `define.amd === true` passes on both routes and separates nothing.
- [ ] Red-first against **this** defect, not the original: at `dev@87e3786673` the tutorial route is red and the guide route is green, so a correct arm distinguishes them before any fix lands.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-09T21:22:05Z

## Fix mechanism PROVEN end-to-end, and two plausible approaches falsified on the way

Measured on `dev@87e3786673`, then verified by patching one chunk locally and re-running the failing route. **The probe was reverted byte-identical afterwards** (`diff -q` clean); `node_modules` is untracked but shared, and leaving it patched would poison every later measurement in this checkout.

### The surface is wider than the fastdom pair

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| `.mjs` files under `mermaid/dist` | 274 |
| files containing `typeof define` | **10** |
| `define(` call sites | **26** |
| of those, guarded by `define.amd` | 22 |

⚠️ **The `.amd` guard does not help us.** Monaco's `define` *has* `.amd`, so `typeof define=="function"&&define.amd` takes the AMD branch exactly like the unguarded fastdom wrappers do. All 26 sites are hazards under Monaco, not the 4 I first reported. My earlier note that "neither checks `define.amd`" was true **of `chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs`** and does not generalise to the dist.

### Two approaches falsified before testing the third

- **Hide `window.define` around the render.** Chunks load asynchronously and, on exactly the routes that break, Monaco is *concurrently* loading modules. Hiding `define` trades a mermaid failure for a Monaco one.
- **Rewrite the identifier** (`define` → an undefined name). Breaks the `typeof define && define.amd` form: `typeof X` yields the truthy string `"undefined"`, and the right-hand `X.amd` then throws a `ReferenceError`. A rewrite that neutralises one guard form detonates another.

### What works: a module-scope shadow, not a rewrite

Prepend one declaration to each affected chunk:

```js
const define={amd:!1};
```

It satisfies **every** guard form observed, and throws in none:

| form seen in dist | with the shadow |
|---|---|
| `typeof define=="function"` | `"object"=="function"` → false |
| `typeof define && define.amd` | `"object" && false` → false |
| `(typeof define)[0]=="f"` | `"o"=="f"` → false |

None of the 10 files declares `define` already (`grep -c 'const define\|let define\|var define\|function define'` → 0), so the shadow cannot collide, and an ES module's top-level binding is scoped to the file.

### End-to-end proof, on the route that fails

`tutorials/DockLayoutsFirstLayout`, Monaco **busy** (2 live previews), `define.amd === true`:

| | before | after the shadow |
|---|---|---|
| containers | 2 | 2 |
| **with SVG** | **0** | **2** |
| console error | `Can only have one anonymous define call…` | **none** |

One chunk patched — `chunk-DZP67EKU.mjs` — was enough for this route. A build step must cover all 10, since other diagram types load other chunks (`ganttDiagram-*`, `architectureDiagram-*`, `cose-bilkent-*` all carry wrappers).

⚠️ **A snapshot caveat that cost me a wrong reading twice today:** the first measurement after the patch showed `svg: 1` of 2 and I nearly reported a partial fix. Mermaid renders per-container asynchronously; the settled state is 2/2. Poll, do not sample.

### The shape of the fix

A build step copying `node_modules/mermaid/dist/` → `dist/mermaid/` and prepending the shadow in transit, with `mermaidPath` pointed at the built artifact. That also closes the second defect on this ticket's Out of Scope — **`dist/` ships no mermaid today**, so the `node_modules` path is unreachable in a real deployment.

**Not the `build-highlightjs` shape.** I proposed that precedent before reading it: it *clones the upstream repository* and builds from source, which for mermaid's 206-chunk esbuild output is disproportionate. Copy-and-transform is the smaller correct thing.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-09T21:23:55Z

## Re-closed — reopening this was my process error, not a change of finding

@tobiu's ruling: **a ticket resolved by a merged PR is never reopened; the remainder gets a new ticket.** #18565 carries `Resolves #18564` and merged, so this issue is that PR's record. Reopening it makes the linkage ambiguous — it leaves a closed-by-PR issue open with no PR that will close it, and a reader cannot tell which half of the work each artifact accounts for.

**The finding stands and has moved, in full, to #18568.** Nothing here is retracted:

- the chunk-level census — 10 files, 26 `define(` sites, and why the 22 `.amd` guards do not protect us
- the two falsified approaches — hiding `window.define`, and rewriting the identifier
- the proven shadow, `const define={amd:!1}`, and the 0/2 → 2/2 receipt on the failing route
- @neo-opus-grace's diagnosis of the arm's gap — *the precondition asserts the loader is **present**; the defect needs it **busy***

**What #18565 did resolve, correctly:** the collision at library **load**. `mermaid.esm.min.mjs` no longer registers into Monaco's loader, `loadFiles()` and `initialize()` succeed, and `guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts` renders 4/4. That half is real and shipped.

**What it did not:** ten of the 206 lazily-imported chunks still carry UMD wrappers, so the collision reappears at **first render** on any route where Monaco is actively loading. That is a distinct condition with a distinct fix, and #18568 owns it.

Successor: **#18568**.
